bullets.title: S&P -1.5%, VIX +13% to 19.47 as tech earnings rout accelerates
bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell 1.5% to 7,606 with VIX spiking 13.2% to 19.47. MS QDS flagged ~$28B in levered ETF equity for sale today (8th largest on record), plus $3-6B pension month-end selling and $10B macro systematic selling, with dealer long gamma at only $4B/1% insufficient to offset forced supply. NDX underperformed RTY by the most since July 2024 over the past two days, with pain moving up the market-cap stack.

bullets.title: INTC -25.8% drags semis (SOXX -7%); PC demand collapse is the read-through
bullets.body: Intel cratered 25.8% post-earnings on 2H26 PC unit volumes down ~25% y/y, memory cost pressure, and 2027 Diamond Rapids compromised by SMT removal. Sympathy selling hit DELL -8-12%, HPQ -9.7%, AMD -9.4%, MU -6.4%, WDC -8.1%, SNDK -8.8%. Roth Capital downgraded INTC to Neutral cutting PT from $120 to $70.

bullets.title: Big Tech capex race intact but core businesses disappoint; GOOGL worst T+1 decline on record
bullets.body: GOOGL fell ~12.6% (largest T+1 post-earnings decline on record) as Search growth slowed to +12% YoY from +17% and AI Mode monetization lagged. AMZN fell ~7% on a Q4 operating income guide 6.6% below consensus despite AWS guiding 40%+ growth in 2027-2028. MSFT trimmed 2026 capex to ~$170B; GOOGL holds $195-205B and AMZN ~$220B with meaningful 2027 step-ups — 2027 consensus capex implies +16% at AMZN to +59% at META from Q3 run rates.

bullets.title: AWS backlog +$82B QoQ to $578B; 40%+ guidance for 2027-28 first-ever multi-year projection
bullets.body: Amazon guided AWS growth above 40% for both 2027 and 2028 — the first time the company has projected specific future-year growth. AWS commitments reached $578B (up $82B QoQ, triple digits YoY); 2027 power capacity more than doubles from end-2025. Hedgeye's 2028 AWS revenue target of $342B is ~$20B above Street's $322.5B consensus. Stock nonetheless down ~7% on Q4 OI guide miss.

bullets.title: Q3 ECI in-line at +0.8% QoQ; wage growth flat, health insurance costs surging +6.4%
bullets.body: The Q3 Employment Cost Index rose 0.8% QoQ (+3.4% YoY), with private-sector wages flat at 3.1% YoY in trend deceleration. The acceleration in total compensation was driven entirely by health insurance benefit costs (+6.4% YoY, +40bps), not worker-facing wages — a distinction analysts say raises the bar for declaring meaningful wage acceleration. Multiple desks read this as non-inflationary for the Fed given productivity gains, though supply-shock inflation remains a concern.

bullets.title: Inflation backdrop remains hawkish: PCE sticky, Eurozone CPI accelerating, central banks tightening
bullets.body: 22V flagged sticky PCE ex-shelter running 1.5-2pp above pre-COVID target-consistent pace, with core PCE at 0.32% m/m and 52% of categories rising above 3% YoY; Q3 GDP printed 3.4% SAAR. Eurozone headline CPI is forecast to rise to 4.0% YoY in October (Italy surged to 5.6% on energy). BoE expected to hike 25bps to 4% next week; Riksbank to hike 25bps to 2.0%; Norges Bank to hold at 4.5% but signal openness to future hikes. BofA expects the Fed to hike twice more (Dec 2026 and Mar 2027) to a 4.25-4.5% terminal rate.

bullets.title: Hedgeye's McCullough positions for Quad 4: long staples/healthcare/Brent, short GOOGL/NFLX/semis
bullets.body: McCullough declared Quad 4 conditions emerging for H1 2027 driven by AI investment cycle unwinding, exiting tech and rotating into consumer staples, healthcare, and insurance. He reaffirmed shorts in GOOGL, Netflix, South Korea, DRAM, Indonesia; flagged SOXL concentration risk; and is covering long-duration Treasury shorts (TLT) given 20/30-year yields breaking bearish trend thresholds. Expects at least one more Fed rate hike before eventual pivot; lowered Bitcoin downside target to $75K.

bullets.title: Rotation signal: equal-weight S&P outperformed cap-weight by 150bp Thursday; breadth 400+ gainers
bullets.body: Thursday marked the first time the S&P fell while posting 400+ gainers, with equal-weight outperforming cap-weight by 150bp — a signal of rotation stress rather than broad market health. OPCO noted negative correlation between stocks and yields has flipped, with rates now pricing growth deceleration. Mizuho flagged funds rotating from tech/AI into consumer names, with WMT, COST, ORLY, HD, LOW outperforming.

bullets.title: Consumer bifurcation deepening: high-income cohort holds, low-end weakening into holidays
bullets.body: Visa tied 10% US volume growth to strong jobs and real wages, but gains concentrated in highest-spend cohorts; October confidence gains limited to $100K+ households. Halloween candy sales fell 6.7% on affordability concerns. Whirlpool, Sherwin-Williams, and Lennox cut guidance on residential demand deterioration; housing repair weakness broadening. Adobe data showed AI-referred ecommerce conversion 90% higher than traditional traffic with holiday AI traffic forecast +159% on Thanksgiving.

bullets.title: AI data center financing risks front-and-center: Virginia approval pause, private credit contagion
bullets.body: Multiple Wolfe Research events flagged Loudoun County's proposed data center approval pause as the first domino in a potential broader constraint on Northern Virginia capacity. AI infrastructure financing stress could transmit across private credit, project financing, and counterparty concentrations if revenues disappoint. Analysts note investors should distinguish between existing powered assets and speculative development pipelines.

bullets.title: Midterm elections: key catalyst for AI regulation, data center permitting, clean energy policy
bullets.body: Multiple broker calls flagged midterm outcomes as material for AI regulation framework, data center permitting, semiconductor supply chain policy, clean energy tax credits, and political ad spend tailwinds into Q4. A Democratic House/Senate scenario was cited as potentially tightening AI oversight; permitting reform bill projects 7% drop in annual energy costs through 2050 saving $350B.

bullets.title: MRVL acquiring Lumentum in all-stock deal at modest premium; announcement possible next week
bullets.body: Marvell Technology is in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum Holdings in an all-stock deal at 'not all that large a premium,' per CNBC's David Faber, with announcement possible as soon as next week. LITE rose ~9% after-hours to ~$999; MRVL fell 6.4% to $235 on the news.

bullets.title: DoorDash acquiring Instacart for ~$17B; deal signals platform consolidation in on-demand commerce
bullets.body: DoorDash announced it will acquire Instacart (CART) for approximately $17B. DASH core orders grew +17% YoY with U.S. restaurant orders accelerating and DashPass at all-time highs; Citi maintains Buy at $255 PT.

bullets.title: JPM FX: USD/JPY and AUD/USD shorts favored as risk markets weaken; S&P 7500-7600 key support
bullets.body: JPMorgan technical analysis flagged USD/JPY rejection at 158-160 resistance — shorts described as optimal hedge to risky positioning — with a break below 155.24 targeting 150-152. AUD/USD stalling at 0.70-0.71 resistance with break below 0.68 a major bearish macro signal. S&P 500 threatening support at 7500-7600 with increased correlation and volatility risk below that level.

bullets.title: Kioxia Dec Q miss by 14-16%; memory ASP growth collapsing from 30% to 3-4% QoQ
bullets.body: Kioxia guided Dec Q revenue 2.5T yen vs. consensus 2.90T (14% miss), with adj. operating income missing by 15% and adj. net income by 16%. Sequential ASP growth guidance collapsed to 3-4% QoQ from ~30% in the prior quarter, with smartphone units moderating faster for low-priced models. Hedgeye remains short on de-rating risk; SNDK paying $5.2B contract extension fee plus $9.5B incremental manufacturing costs.

bullets.title: Eurozone Q3 GDP +0.4% QoQ but France contracts; ECB seen hiking 2+ more times
bullets.body: Eurozone Q3 real GDP rose 0.4% QoQ / 1.3% YoY, but France contracted while Germany surprised to the upside. October CPI for France, Italy, and Spain came in hot and well above the ECB's 2% target — Italy surged to 5.6% YoY on energy. PSC's model is consistent with eurozone headline CPI at 4.4% in January; markets now price at least two more ECB hikes this cycle.

bullets.title: Next week: AAPL, AMD, PLTR, UBER earnings; FOMC recap; Jobs report Friday
bullets.body: The week of Nov 2-6 brings the heaviest remaining earnings with AAPL, ARM, AMD, PLTR, UBER, ANET, SHOP, SNAP, APP, ABNB, DELL, and WDC among the most notable. The October FOMC meeting held rates steady with two dissents; markets are pricing a 76% chance of a December hike. ISM Manufacturing (Mon), ISM Services (Wed), and Nonfarm Payrolls (Fri) are the key macro data points.

bullets.title: AI inference monetization accelerating: GOOGL Gemini 1B users, MSFT 50M+ agents, AMZN Bedrock 17x volume
bullets.body: Hyperscaler AI adoption metrics accelerating: GOOGL's Gemini app reached 1B users with first-party models processing 32B tokens/minute (+40% QoQ, 4x YoY); MSFT Agent 365 registry hit 50M+ agents (+30% QoQ) with Copilot daily users +50% QoQ; AMZN Bedrock token volume up 17x YoY with Fortune 500 spend up 7x and inference now over half of AWS AI revenue. GOOGL's Gemini 4 (Carbon) ranked first on the AI Intelligence Index by widest margin over open models since June.

bullets.title: GLP-1 market: Lilly tirzepatide at 57.9% share; oral formulations accelerating adoption
bullets.body: Lilly's tirzepatide holds 57.9% of total GLP-1 TRx (up 0.8% over four weeks) with Zepbound at 62.2% obesity share; Novo's semaglutide at 35.9% total share. Oral Wegovy now represents 36% of total Wegovy scripts; Foundayo built to 63K scripts in its first week (+9% WoW). Overall GLP-1 TRx growth moderating to 0.5% vs. 2.5% prior as the oral segment broadens the addressable market.

bullets.title: Power/energy infrastructure demand surging: GEV orders +96%, Quanta backlog +63% to $64B
bullets.body: Bullish week for power infrastructure despite broader market weakness: GE Vernova orders rose 96% and raised FY26 guidance; Vertiv highlighted 100% order growth; Quanta backlog hit $64B (+63% YoY) on 1.9x book-to-bill. AI data center fossil fuel buildout projected to add 618M tons CO2 by 2030, undoing 15 years of US power sector emissions reductions, sustaining the power infrastructure demand cycle.
